theory: The sine-angle rule fails for negative values: with the principal angle $\alpha=\arcsin(p)$, use $\alpha+2\pi n$ and $\pi-\alpha+2\pi n$, retaining all angles in the domain; endpoint and repeated-root cases must be handled. State $a>0$ for the period formula, or use $2\pi/|a|$ for $a\ne0$. Duration above a level requires identifying every qualifying interval, including intervals adjoining domain endpoints; it is not always the interval between two crossings. Replace the blanket claim that a model is only reliable within its measurement span with a qualified statement that extrapolation depends on whether its assumptions continue to hold.
